knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Compiler shape validation diverges from eager semantics for zeroed-out optional operands
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: When an operation has coefficients that make an operand semantically unused, eager execution may skip shape validation for that operand, while graph compilers may still perform full shape validation and reject programs that eager execution accepts.

risk_dimensions.shape: Optional or coefficient-disabled operand shapes that are not broadcastable to the operation output
risk_dimensions.device: Backend compilation paths that perform graph-level shape validation
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Compiled execution with full graph tracing, especially when coefficients disable operand contributions

failure_mechanism.description: Graph compilers may enforce broadcasting or shape compatibility for all operands even when eager semantics would ignore an operand whose contribution is zeroed out by a coefficient, causing compilation failures for programs that are valid in eager mode.

input_exploration: Vary coefficients that may disable operand contributions, especially zero-valued coefficients
Explore operand shapes that are not broadcastable to the output shape
Vary matrix and tensor dimensions to cover mismatched broadcasting relationships
Exercise both eager and compiled execution paths with the same inputs
constraint_awareness: Eager execution may skip shape validation for semantically disabled operands, while compilers may not preserve this behavior
Full graph compilation can make compiler shape validation stricter than partial graph execution
Backend selection can change whether shape validation failures are raised
oracle_strategy: Compare eager execution against compiled execution and flag cases where eager succeeds but compilation raises an exception
Monitor for compiler shape broadcasting failures
Use differential execution as the primary correctness signal

transferability.reason: The principle that compilers may not preserve eager short-circuit semantics for coefficient-disabled or optional operands applies broadly to operations with optional tensor arguments or scaling coefficients, beyond the original API.

important_considerations: Focus on operations where optional or coefficient-disabled operands may be excluded at runtime
Vary compiler backends, full graph settings, and device types
Combine shape incompatibility with zero-valued coefficients to expose semantic mismatch
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that run the same operation under eager and compiled execution modes, create mismatched optional operand shapes, vary coefficients that can disable operand contributions, and compare success or failure without copying the original historical reproduction.
